misconceptions.description: Feeding TeachGen@i a generic scenario such as "plan a math lesson" without grade band, prior knowledge, class size, or constraints
misconceptions.trigger: the prompt names a topic but omits the learners, the setting, and what they already know
misconceptions.feedback: A scenario the AI can plan for names the grade, the prior lesson, the time block, and at least one constraint. Generic in means generic out.

misconceptions.description: Inventing convenient student traits or pasting identifiable student records into the scenario to get a tailored plan
misconceptions.trigger: scenario adds specific named students, IEP details, or real assessment data to the prompt
misconceptions.feedback: Describe learner needs in de-identified, aggregate terms. Never paste identifiable student records into a generative tool.

misconceptions.description: Setting up the scenario without the binding constraints and only noticing them after the AI returns an unusable plan
misconceptions.trigger: teacher generates a plan, then discovers it ignores the 40-minute block, the no-devices rule, or the standard being assessed
misconceptions.feedback: Put the hard constraints into the scenario first. A plan built on missing constraints is fluent but not usable.
